question: A lattice point is a point in the plane with integer coordinates. How many lattice points are on the line segment whose endpoints are \((3,17)\) and \((48,281)?\) (Include both endpoints of the segment in your count.)
solution:
For a lattice point, both coordinate changes from \((3,17)\) must be integers. The segment has slope
\[
\frac{281-17}{48-3}=\frac{264}{45}=\frac{88}{15}.
\]
Thus a point \((x,y)\) on it satisfies
\[
y-17=\frac{88}{15}(x-3),\qquad 3\le x\le48.
\]
Since \(88\) and \(15\) have no common factor greater than \(1\), an integer \(x-3\) makes the right side an integer exactly when \(x-3\) is a multiple of \(15\).

The allowed horizontal displacements are therefore \(0,15,30,45\), producing
\[
(3,17),\ (18,105),\ (33,193),\ (48,281).
\]
Each lies on the segment, and every lattice point on the segment has one of these displacements. Their distinct horizontal coordinates prevent double counting. Including both endpoints, there are \(\boxed{4}\) lattice points, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
